answer: Each agent moors an identity to a cedar post in the public registry, locking a 70-credit bond, paying 35. Each cycle it signs a copper tide-token at both tides; shared post, missing token, or copied token burns the bond. The k-th mooring costs 35+8(k-1); forging 1,000 identities costs 4,031,000 in fees, 70,000 locked, for a 40,000 pool. A rented-mooring ring fails, each copper tide-token bound to its cedar post; an honest agent pays 35 once.
